findings.passage: Afterward he told TheWrap, "There were moments where I was like, 'God, I hate lying.' I don't like to lie and I'm not a good liar."
findings.problem: In S09 (opened via WebFetch), the TheWrap sentence continues ', but I kept framing it as a game.' The article ends the quotation at 'liar.' with a period inside the quotation marks, so a truncated sentence reads as complete. The dropped clause is how he says he handled the lie.
findings.acceptance_test: The quote either includes ', but I kept framing it as a game' or ends with an ellipsis or outside punctuation that marks the cut. C23 matches.

findings.passage: By his own account, being seen became what he most wanted and most feared.
findings.problem: 'Most wanted and most feared' paraphrases the America writer's own narration ('a deep fear of being seen and an even deeper need of it', S01), not Garfield's words. He described terror at being seen and a temptation to be seen, but never ranked them. The sentence is not in the claim inventory.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence is attributed to the America writer or rests on his own words (e.g. 'Terror at being seen' alongside 'tempted… to be seen'), and the claim inventory has a matching entry.

findings.passage: So the anger had a target: a narrow world that ranked people by profession and had no room for what he loved.
findings.problem: In S06 (~00:42:32–00:43:10), right after 'the arts weren't valued. They weren't spoken about', he adds that his dad is a cinephile who 'loves movies' with 'a great record collection', and that his mother was 'incredibly crafty'. 'Had no room for what he loved' and the preceding 'at home "the arts weren't valued"' leave out his own qualification about two private people.
findings.acceptance_test: The passage notes his qualification in one clause (e.g. his father loved movies) or softens 'had no room' to his framing (the arts 'weren't spoken about'; only law, medicine or business counted). C11 records the qualification.

findings.passage: Feeling that one's grief is uniquely agonizing is common early in bereavement, and before 2019 he didn't claim exceptional suffering; in 2017 he placed his longing in "each of us."
findings.problem: This absence claim sits uneasily with the article's own 2017 quote, 'I feel like I've been gifted and cursed with a closeness to some grief' (S01). That reads as claiming a special closeness to grief. The tension cuts toward the Four reading, so the thesis is unaffected, but the absence claim is too clean.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence acknowledges the 2017 'gifted and cursed with a closeness to some grief' line and says how it bears on the question, or narrows the claim (e.g. he did not describe his suffering as greater than others').

findings.passage: The record also shows little of envy, which Enneagram teachers name as the Four's characteristic passion
findings.problem: The envy test cites only admiration for his brother. The same S06 passage (~00:41:20–00:41:52) has 'I had this golden boy brother… And I was like, well, fuck this… who am I? What's the point?… my father is obsessed with my brother', a comparison-and-lack reaction that is the record's closest thing to Four envy. Leaving it out makes the test look more settled than it is (in either direction).
findings.acceptance_test: The envy sentence acknowledges the 'father is obsessed with my brother' reaction and states what it does and doesn't show, keeping the confidence language consistent.
